questions.prompt: Locke’s “idea,” in the line Bonevac quotes, is:
choices: A Only innate Platonic Forms.
B Whatsoever is the object of the understanding when a man thinks.
C Only public language tokens.
D Brain neurons exclusively.

questions.prompt: Empiricists allow analytic a priori knowledge as:
choices: A Synthetic insights about causation.
B Verbal/definitional truths independent of experience (e.g., bachelors are unmarried).
C Innate geometry of space only.
D Revelatory mysticism.

questions.prompt: If an alleged idea can’t be traced to impressions, Hume’s verdict is:
choices: A It is necessarily true.
B Discard it—without impression-trace it lacks content.
C It must be innate.
D It is a mathematical axiom.

questions.prompt: Hume’s Treatise, in his later words:
choices: A Made him instantly rich and famous.
B Fell stillborn from the press.
C Was banned from all libraries permanently.
D Was co-authored with Locke.

questions.prompt: Versus Leibniz’s synthetic a priori, Hume says causal expectation is:
choices: A Pure rational insight.
B Not rationally founded—a feeling of expectation/custom.
C Analytic verbal truth only.
D Direct perception of necessary connection.
